title: Oncall Decision Briefs and Severity Calibration
author: Lina Rodriguez
content:
Summary:
This page is a compact, action-oriented set of decision briefs for oncall leads and bridge operators to calibrate incident severity, accelerate correct containment actions, and produce consistent customer communications. It contains: a severity calibration matrix tuned for LLM serving, short decision briefs per common signal, a 10-step incident containment runbook skeleton, rotation expectations and handoff checklist, a library of lightweight game-day scenarios, and ready-to-send status & post-incident templates.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: Redwood Inference public-facing services and customer-dedicated model pools.
- Intent: reduce ambiguity during initial 0–30 minute response window; help oncall quickly select severity, route resources, and produce customer-safe notices.

Quick definitions:
- Pager: immediate interrupt for a responder.
- Bridge: the primary coordination channel (Zoom + Slack bridge).
- IC: Incident Commander.
- SLO breach: measurable deviation for latency, availability, or quality.

Severity calibration matrix (use within first 10 minutes):
| Severity | Observable signal (example) | Immediate action (first 10m) | Pager? | Exec notify? |
|---|---|---:|:---:|:---:|
| Sev 1 (Critical) | Multi-region 5xx surge > 3x baseline OR >2% customer-impacting errors for 15m | Open bridge, notify SRE and sysadmin, failover/rollback to previous model, trigger capacity uplift | Yes (all hands) | Yes (CTO, Head of SRE) |
| Sev 2 (High) | Sustained 99.9th percentile token latency increase >2x for >10m OR major customer tenant errors | Open bridge, short-term throttles, enable cached responses, engage model team | Yes | No (exec watch) |
| Sev 3 (Medium) | Intermittent latency spikes, elevated error traces localized to a pool | Triage oncall, collect traces, apply targeted restarts, monitor | Maybe (rotation-dependent) | No |
| Sev 4 (Low) | Degraded observability, single non-prod pool flake, or advisory quality regression | File ticket, schedule follow-up, run diagnostic job | No | No |

How to pick the right severity (decision brief):
1) Measure customer impact: count of affected requests, percentage error rate, and whether any SLA/commitment is violated.
2) Confirm signal covariance: is latency accompanied by increased CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache evictions, or network errors?
3) Consider blast radius: single tenant, single region, or global?
4) Choose severity that matches SLO impact and blast radius; document reasons on the bridge.

Immediate containment runbook (0–30 minutes):
1. Acknowledge pager within 2 minutes and post initial stub in bridge: cause-known? impact-estimate? immediate-actions? IC: <name>.
2. Collect telemetry: run quick queries (examples below).
3. Isolate scope: identify affected model, region, and tenant(s).
4. If errors > threshold or global latency: route traffic to standby region or compatible model variant.
5. Apply temporary rate-limiting per-tenant or increase token budget for critical customers.
6. If KV cache thrash: increase cache size or flush hot keys; roll-back recent cache config changes.
7. If GPU saturations: scale up Dedicated pool or enable burst capacity; drain noisy pods.
8. If model quality regression suspected: switch to previous model version (pin) and disable canary.
9. Validate core functionality with synthetic smoke tests (examples below).
10. Stabilize and move to recovery playbook; document timeline.

Quick telemetry commands (examples for bridge use):
- kubectl get pods -n serving -l pool=model-x -o wide
- ./infra/ops/bin/query_metrics --metric=token_latency_99 --window=10m --service=serving
- curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://admin.redwood/api/pools/active | jq
- python tools/run_smoke.py --endpoint=https://host/compose --prompt-file=smoke/prompts/basic.json

Validation & smoke tests (3 checks):
- Latency smoke: execute 20 small inference requests, confirm p50 < expected and p99 < threshold.
- Throughput smoke: run a 60s burst to confirm autoscaler behavior and observe error rate.
- Quality smoke: run 10 golden prompts from eval set and diff token-level outputs vs baseline.

Handoff and rotation expectations:
- Primary oncall should hold the bridge for first 30–60 minutes. After stabilization, IC names the continuity owner for long-tail remediation.
- Handoff checklist (pre-handover): current severity, actions taken, open tasks, key leads and their contact, expected next check-in time, link to postmortem stub.
- Shadow policy: second-level oncall must be shadowing high-severity incidents until bridge is closed.

Game-day scenario library (pick 1–2 per 90m drill):
- Scenario A: Global KV cache evictions triggered by heavy prompt prefixes; objective: restore tail latency to 95% of baseline in 30m. Success criteria: p99 latency reduced to target and no customer SLA violations.
- Scenario B: Canary model rollout introduces hallucination spike for a subset of prompts; objective: detect quality regression, rollback, and verify. Success: rollback within 15m, zero impacted customers in next hour.
- Scenario C: Bursty token flood from multi-tenant misconfiguration leading to GPU saturation; objective: apply tenant throttles and bring utilization under 85% in 20m.
- Scoring rubric: detection time (0–10), containment time (0–20), correctness of customer comms (0–5), post-incident documentation (0–5).

Customer & status page templates (use during first 60 minutes):
- Short status (public):
  Title: "Partial service disruption affecting model inference in <region>"
  Status: Investigating / Identified / Mitigating / Resolved
  Impact: "Some customers may experience increased latency or errors for text generation in <region>."
  Next update: "<time in UTC; e.g., 2026-01-15T15:45Z>"

- Internal customer notice (email/CSR):
  Subject: [Incident] Degraded inference throughput in <region> — immediate actions taken
  Body: "Timeline: <brief timeline>. Impact: <who/what>. Actions taken: switched traffic to fallback model, enabled per-tenant throttles. Next steps: continuing validation and a follow-up at <time>. If you see critical customer impact, reply to this thread and we will prioritize outreach. — Oncall team"

Post-incident (30–120 minutes after stabilization):
- Evidence collection: attach traces, dashboard snapshots (token_latency, error_rate, cpu/gpu_util), and command history.
- Immediate remediation tickets: create JIRA with severity, owner, ETA for fix and link to postmortem.
- Postmortem stub: use the Incident comm and postmortem framework page (link included below) and ensure RCA distinguishes cause vs trigger.

Calibration checklist for oncall leads (weekly):
- Review all Sev1/Sev2 incidents from last week and confirm severity assignments.
- Re-run 1 game-day scenario with the current oncall roster.
- Audit status page templates used and sample the last 3 customer notices for tone and completeness.
- Confirm runbook commands remain executable and update credentials if needed.

Runbook maintenance rules:
- Every change to a critical runbook requires a PR, peer reviewer, and one successful game-day validation.
- Runbooks older than 180 days must be flagged for review.

- Operator competency & evidence handbook: <confluence://operator-competency-incident-evidence-handbook-2025>

Ownership and escalation paths:
- Primary: Serving SRE (oncall rotation) — first responder & bridge operator.
- Secondary: Runtime team — model/pool experts.
- Tertiary: Customer success for high-touch customers and legal for any regulatory-impacting incidents.

Revision history:
- 2025-02-10: initial draft by Lina Rodriguez.
- 2025-05-04: added KV cache guidance and smoke tests (reviewers updated).
- 2026-01-15: calibration checklist and new game-day scenarios added (published).

Notes for readers:
- Use this page as a living playbook; pick the severity conservatively if in doubt and prioritize customer safety.
- If you have changes, open a PR against the runbook repository and ping the reviewers listed on this page.
